The notes indicate the deal was actively advancing through Microsoft sourcing, legal, and approval workflows during June 2026. The primary focus was finalizing the Letter of Authorization (LOA) and securing Microsoft internal approvals.

- 6/17/2026:
  - Cisco presented the offer to Microsoft.
  - The Azure team reportedly responded positively.

- 6/22/2026:
  - LOA preparation was underway and expected by 6/24.
  - Microsoft planned a senior review approval discussion on 6/25.
  - Cisco teams were simultaneously preparing sourcing collateral and coordinating approvals.

- 6/25/2026:
  - John Glass (Sourcing GM) approved the deal to proceed prior to SSR review.
  - Initial LOA documentation was provided.

- 6/26/2026:
  - Microsoft sourcing returned redlines on the LOA.

- 6/27/2026:
  - Cisco responded to the redlines.
  - The LOA advanced into Microsoft Legal review.

Commercial and operational observations:
- The projected booking date consistently remained 7/24/2026.
- The transaction required eight approvals, creating timeline sensitivity and execution risk.
- Notes referenced “large attrition” impacts related to accounting and revenue timing:
  - Only six months of services revenue would initially be recognized.
  - The remaining six months were expected to shift into Q4 FY27.
- On 6/15/2026, the opportunity was identified as being at risk of missing FY26 booking because of the compressed LOA approval timeline.
- The notes also stated that if the upgrade did not proceed, the renewal itself was still expected to close in Q2 FY27 without major concern.
